D.t: Lynne Walz trails by 4.5 and wins 19% of simulations. Closing it takes about 17,596 voters switching sides, or 35,191 more net votes from new turnout.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between R +11.1 and D +2.1. A normal polling error decides it.

The polls page average is R +4.4. Your best recent poll is Concord Public Opinion Partners for Education Reform Now Advocacy (D) at D +0.3; your worst is Echelon Insights for NetChoice at R +7.3. 9 polls in the last 30 days.

The biggest vote banks for Democrats: Douglas, a projected net 67,220 votes; Lancaster, a projected net 32,518 votes; Sarpy, a projected net 5,905 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: Sarpy, D +7.6, 10.0% of the vote.

D.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
D.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Lynne Walz runs furthest behind in Platte, Madison, Washington. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: White voters, 90% of voters, 42 to 52, where a 5 point gain is worth 4.50 points; Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 70% of voters, 44 to 50, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.48 points; Voters who find daily costs hard to afford, 60% of voters, 47 to 47, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.02 points.
The forecast's worst groups for Lynne Walz: Immigration voters 15 to 80, Small counties 26 to 67, Incomes $125K and up 40 to 54. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
$860K cash against $7.5M. Outspent: lean on earned media, digital, field and the outside groups, and pick the two or three media markets that decide it.
Registered Democrats cast 40% of the 185,194 ballots in Nebraska so far, against 43% for the other party. That is 5.7 points better for Democrats than the forecast expected by now.

D.h: What the ballots so far say
D.t: The early vote has moved this forecast 0.1 points toward Lynne Walz. Bank it: chase the remaining mail ballots and low propensity voters who have not voted.
Cash: $7.5M in the bank against $860K for Lynne Walz.

R.t: Jim Pillen leads by 4.5 in the forecast and wins 81% of simulations. The cushion is about 35,191 votes; a one point swing is about 3,876 voters changing sides.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between D +2.1 and R +11.1. A normal polling error decides it.

The polls page average is R +4.4. Your best recent poll is Echelon Insights for NetChoice at R +7.3; your worst is Concord Public Opinion Partners for Education Reform Now Advocacy (D) at D +0.3. 9 polls in the last 30 days.

The biggest vote banks for Republicans: Platte, a projected net 6,910 votes; Madison, a projected net 6,267 votes; Lincoln, a projected net 5,694 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: Sarpy, D +7.6, 10.0% of the vote.

R.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
R.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Jim Pillen runs furthest behind in Lancaster, Douglas, Sarpy. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: White voters, 90% of voters, 52 to 42, where a 5 point gain is worth 4.50 points; Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 70% of voters, 50 to 44, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.48 points; Voters who find daily costs hard to afford, 60% of voters, 47 to 47, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.02 points.
The forecast's worst groups for Jim Pillen: Independents 23 to 66, 2024 nonvoters and third party voters 30 to 63, Moderates 32 to 60. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
$7.5M cash against $860K. Spend it early on persuasion television in the battleground counties and keep a reserve for the last week.
Registered Republicans cast 43% of the 185,194 ballots in Nebraska so far, against 40% for the other party. That is 5.7 points worse for Republicans than the forecast expected by now.

R.h: What the ballots so far say
R.t: The early vote has moved this forecast 0.1 points away from Jim Pillen. Election Day has to make it up: the remaining vote must break harder your way than the forecast expects.
